findings.reason: The new handler calls privileges.global.can('groups:view:users', uid). Repository privilege helpers add their own 'groups:' prefix when checking group grants, so this looks up a different key from the granted groups:view:users permission; authorized guests and users cannot receive the required 200 WebFinger response.

The new router registers controllers['well-known'].webfinger, but src/controllers/index.js does not export 'well-known'. Its registration therefore supplies an undefined Express callback, making the route unusable and causing startup to fail once mounted.

Rewriting src/routes/well-known.js retained the registration through controllers['well-known'].webfinger without adding that controller to src/controllers/index.js or using a valid passed controller. The repeated undefined callback still prevents WebFinger registration.

Adding wellKnownRoutes(router, middleware, controllers) to addCoreRoutes makes startup execute the invalid registration from steps 79 and 98. Express receives an undefined WebFinger callback, breaking application route initialization rather than merely leaving the new endpoint unavailable.

The added integration tests cannot validate the implementation as written: their before hook calls User.getSlug, which is not defined in src/user, and request-promise calls expecting 400/403/404 omit simple:false, so they reject before status assertions. The success test also expects a uid: alias while the handler generates a /uid/ URL. These mismatches leave the new behavior without usable test coverage.

run_review.reason: The completed official evaluation reports unresolved, with all four WebFinger tests and all 182 preservation tests failing. The router mounts an undefined controllers['well-known'].webfinger because src/controllers/index.js never exports the new controller, preventing route startup. Independently, the handler checks privileges.global.can('groups:view:users', uid) rather than the privilege key 'view:users', so authorized requests would be denied even after registration is fixed.

findings.reason: The `/tmp/probe3.js` require-tracing script continued a series of standalone-loading probes after step 86 had shown that loading the existing controllers also exited outside bootstrap. Tracing the exit through `src/meta` and its database dependency did not verify the new route; switching to `node --check` and the bootstrapped test harness, as the agent subsequently did, was cheaper.

After the `setsid nohup` launch at step 112 had appeared healthy but Redis was unavailable for the test at step 114, the agent tried another detached `setsid nohup redis-server` launch; this one also reported that `disown` was unavailable. Starting Redis and running Mocha within one shell call was the cheaper way to test without relying on persistence between calls.

The agent reran `npx mocha test/well-known.js` in a separate shell call after the detached-Redis approach had already produced `ECONNREFUSED` at step 114. The intervening `redis-cli ping` only established availability at that moment, just as the earlier ping had; the repeated run again failed before tests executed. Running Redis alongside the test in one call would have avoided this extra failed suite invocation.
